
# 2. Data selection

This section describes the data selection process. It starts with the seven data files described above, selects the analysis relevant variables from each data file, and then saves them as intermediate data files for later use.  Data are selected across four HRS waves (2016, 2018, 2020, 2022).



## Input Data

| Object | Source File | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `tracker` | `A0_005_tracker.rds` | HRS tracker file (sampling, demographics, weights) |
| `h16a_r` | `A0_005_h16a_r.rds` | HRS 2016 Section A (household/respondent info) |
| `h16d_r` | `A0_005_h16d_r.rds` | HRS 2016 Section D (cognition & function) |
| `h16g_r` | `A0_005_h16g_r.rds` | HRS 2016 Section G (IADL) |
| `normexcld` | `A0_005_normexcld.rds` | Normative exclusion flags |
| `hrshcap` | `A0_005_hrshcap.rds` | HCAP clinical diagnosis & domain scores |
| `hc16hp_r` | `A0_005_hc16hp_r.rds` | HCAP 2016 sampling weights |
| `hcap_validation` | `A0_005_hcap_validation.rds` | HRS/HCAP validation subsample (N=50) |
| `h18a_r` | `A0_005_h18a_r.rds` | HRS 2018 Section A (household/respondent info) |
| `h18d_r` | `A0_005_h18d_r.rds` | HRS 2018 Section D (cognition & function) |
| `h18g_r` | `A0_005_h18g_r.rds` | HRS 2018 Section G (IADL) |
| `h20a_r` | `A0_005_h20a_r.rds` | HRS 2020 Section A (household/respondent info) |
| `h20d_r` | `A0_005_h20d_r.rds` | HRS 2020 Section D (cognition & function) |
| `h20g_r` | `A0_005_h20g_r.rds` | HRS 2020 Section G (IADL) |
| `h22a_r` | `A0_005_h22a_r.rds` | HRS 2022 Section A (household/respondent info) |
| `h22d_r` | `A0_005_h22d_r.rds` | HRS 2022 Section D (cognition & function) |
| `h22g_r` | `A0_005_h22g_r.rds` | HRS 2022 Section G (IADL) |

## Processing Steps

### 1. Cognition (`hrs16_cog`)

Variables are selected from each wave's Section D file covering the major cognitive domains assessed in HRS. The same variables are selected across all four waves (with wave-specific prefixes P/Q/R/S):


| Variable(s) | Domain |
|---|---|
| `xD174` | Immediate word recall (10-word list) |
| `xD184` | Delayed word recall |
| `xD151–xD154` | Orientation to time (month, day, year, day of week) |
| `xD124`, `xD129` | Backwards counting from 20 |
| `xD155–xD156` | Object naming (scissors, cactus) |
| `xD157–xD158` | President/vice-president naming |
| `xD142–xD146` | Serial 7s subtraction |
| `xD196`, `xD198` | Additional cognitive items |
| `xNSSCORE` | Nurse/proxy cognitive summary score (2016, 2020, 2022 only) |


For the 2016 wave (`hrs16_cog`), normative exclusion flags from `normexcld` are joined by `HHID`/`PN` to identify respondents who should be excluded from normative cognitive scoring. The 2018 wave data requires renaming of lowercase identifiers (`hhid`, `pn`, `qsubhh`) to match the uppercase convention used across waves.



### 2. HCAP Diagnosis & Domain Flags (`hrshcap`)

Variables are selected from the HCAP dataset covering:

- **Clinical diagnoses:** `vs1hcapdx` (primary), `vs1hcapdxeap` (expert adjudication panel)
- **Domain-level impairment flags** (memory, executive function, language/fluency, visuospatial, orientation) across standard and EAP scoring
- **Additional scales:** JORM informant report (`vs3jormsc_iflag`), Blessed scale (`vs3blessedsc_iflag`)



### 3. HCAP Sampling Weight (`hc16hp_r`)

`HCAP16WGTR` is retained alongside identifiers. 


### 4. HCAP Validation Subsample (`hcap_validation`)

Retains `samplingP` (sampling probability) and `consensuspaneldx` (consensus panel diagnosis) for the N=50 validation subsample. 


### 5. Functional Impairment — ADL (`hrs16_func`)

Variables are selected from `h16d_r` covering:

- `xD101`, `xD102` — Functional difficulty summary items (`PD101` added 2025-07-21)
- `xD502`, `xD505–xD553` — Full battery of ADL/functional limitation items
- `xD554`, `xD555`, `xD556` — Additional functional items (added 2026-05-12)

The same variable set is selected across all four waves.

### 6. Functional Impairment — IADL (`hrs16_iadl`)

Variables are selected from `h16g_r` covering:

- `xG013` — Screener item used to determine IADL skip patterns (`PG013` added 2025-07-26)
- `xG014`, `xG021`, `xG023`, `xG030`, `xG041`, `xG044`, `xG047`, `xG050`, `xG051`, `xG059` — Core IADL battery (dressing, bathing, eating, toileting, meal prep, grocery shopping, phone calls, medications, managing money)
- `xG040` — Map reading item (included in 2016, 2018, 2020 but **not available in 2022**)


### 7. Demographics & Sampling Weights (`tracker_demo`)

Core demographic and design variables are drawn from the tracker file and all four waves' Section A files, then joined together.

**From `tracker`:**

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `SECU`, `STRATUM` | Complex survey design variables |
| `HCAP16RESP` | HCAP 2016 response indicator |
| `PWGTR`–`SWGTR` | HRS person-level weights (all four waves) |
| `xIWTYPE` | Interview type (all four waves) |
| `xAGE` | Age at interview (all four waves) |
| `xINSAMP`, `xIWWAVE`, `xIWYEAR` | Sample/wave/year indicators (all four waves) |
| `xMARST` | Marital status (all four waves) |
| `xNURSHM` | Nursing home residence (all four waves) |
| `xPROXY` | Proxy interview flag (all four waves) |
| `GENDER`, `HISPANIC`, `RACE` | Sex/race/ethnicity |
| `SCHLYRS`, `DEGREE` | Education (years & degree) |
| `BIRTHYR` | Birth year |

**From Section A files (all four waves):**

`xA019` — Current age calculation

All four waves are joined sequentially to `tracker_demo` via `left_join` on `HHID`, `PN`, and the wave-specific sub-household identifier.
